diagrams.title: Electric field lines and an electromagnetic wave
diagrams.cap: Maxwell: a changing E makes B and a changing B makes E, so the wave carries itself at c = 1/√(μ₀ε₀) = 3 × 10⁸ m/s. E, B and the direction of travel are mutually perpendicular.
diagrams.qq: Speed of an EM wave in free space?

diagrams.title: Faraday's law: only the normal component of B links a loop
diagrams.cap: Flux through a loop is the surface integral of B·dA, so for a loop in the XY plane only the z-component of B counts. The induced emf is −dΦ/dt; when the flux contains different frequencies the rms of the emf is the root of the sum of the squares of the individual rms values.
diagrams.qq: B = 0.5(x̂ + ẑ) T on a 0.1 m² loop in the XY plane. Φ?

diagrams.title: Fields of standard charges and currents
diagrams.cap: Gauss's law gives E for symmetric charges (1/r² for a point, 1/r for a line, constant for a sheet) and Ampère's or Biot–Savart's law gives H for currents (I/2πr for a long wire, I/2a at the centre of a loop, nI inside a solenoid).
diagrams.qq: Long wire, 10 A, at 0.5 m. H?

diagrams.title: Boundary conditions, images and capacitance
diagrams.cap: At a boundary the tangential E and normal B are continuous, while normal D jumps by the surface charge and tangential H by the surface current, so field lines bend with tan θ₁/tan θ₂ = ε₁/ε₂. A charge above a grounded plane behaves as if an equal and opposite image charge sat below it.
diagrams.qq: Which component of E is continuous at a boundary?

diagrams.title: Magnetic circuit with an air gap, stored energy and magnet pull
diagrams.cap: A magnetic circuit is solved like a DC circuit: MMF NI drives flux Φ through reluctances l/(µA) in series. A small air gap has far more reluctance than the iron, so it sets the flux, stores most of the energy and gives the pull F = B²A/(2µ₀).
diagrams.qq: B = 1 T over 1 cm². Pull across the gap?

diagrams.title: B–H (hysteresis) loop
diagrams.cap: Loop area = hysteresis loss per cycle per m³. Soft iron (transformers): narrow loop, low H<sub>c</sub>. Hard steel (permanent magnets): wide loop, high B<sub>r</sub> and H<sub>c</sub>.
diagrams.qq: Which material has a narrow loop?

mistakes.m: Gauss's law finds E for any charge arrangement
mistakes.c: It is always true but gives E easily only with symmetry (point, line, sheet, sphere).

mistakes.m: Magnetic field lines start at N and end at S
mistakes.c: B lines are closed loops (∇·B = 0); there are no magnetic charges.

mistakes.m: E inside a charged conductor depends on its charge
mistakes.c: In electrostatics E = 0 inside a conductor; the charge sits on the surface.

mistakes.m: An EMF needs a changing B
mistakes.c: It needs changing flux linkage — changing B, area, orientation, or motion through the field.
